title: Rationalization and finite scalar extension of reconstructed representing pairs
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, and a $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Choose a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{g}Y)$, with $j$ open and $g$ proper [def-weil-compactifications-refinements].

Put $\widehat R_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ and let $\mathcal I_T(R)$ be the completed integral constructible category [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. Use the actual reduction/total-limit adjunction $\mathcal R_T\dashv\mathcal L_T$, $\mathcal L_T=R\varprojlim\operatorname{Res}$, with unit $u$ and counit $e$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Let $P_R:\mathcal I_X(R)\to\mathcal I_Y(R)$ be compact-support reconstruction, with its actual system comparison $\alpha_K:\mathcal R_Y P_RK\xrightarrow{\sim}F\mathcal R_XK$, where $F=Rg_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}$ on pro-etale towers [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization]. Let $L\in\mathcal I_Y(R)$ and let $M_\bullet$, $M=\mathcal L_XM_\bullet$, $\phi_n$, and $t:P_RM\to L$ be supplied exceptional-system data and the reconstructed representing pair of [lem-pur-integral-reconstructed-representing-pair], under either of its two alternatives. Put $J_T:\mathcal I_T(R)[1/t]\simeq\mathcal C_E^c(T)$ for scalar-extension realization [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization], where rationalized morphisms are integral Hom groups tensored with $E$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Write $M_E^c=J_X(M[1/t])$, $L_E^c=J_Y(L[1/t])$ and $P_E^c=Rg_{*,E}j_{!,E}$ on condensed constructible modules [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization]. There are natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_E(C,M_E^c)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_E(P_E^c C,L_E^c)\qquad(C\in\mathcal C_E^c(X)),$$
with counit the realization of $t$.

For any finite $H/E$, write $S=\mathcal O_H$, choose a uniformizer $v$ and write $tS=v^eS$. The ordinary derived extensions $M_S=M\otimes^L_{\widehat R_X}\widehat S_X$, $L_S=L\otimes^L_{\widehat R_Y}\widehat S_Y$ lie in $\mathcal I_X(S)$ and $\mathcal I_Y(S)$ and agree with completed integral extension. The extended map
$$t_S:P_SM_S\xrightarrow{\sim}(P_RM)_S\xrightarrow{t\otimes1}L_S$$
has finite exceptional transpose an isomorphism at every quotient $S/v^m$. At a cofinal quotient $S/v^{en}=S/t^nS$ this transpose is the finite-free extension of $\phi_n$ followed by the canonical finite exceptional mate; its further quotient at any $m\le en$ is the quotient mate applied to this same map. The maps obtained using two cofinal indices agree after their common further comparison.

Let $F_S^{\mathrm{et}}\dashv G_S^{\mathrm{et}}$ be the ordinary Brown tower adjunction over the $v$-power system of [lem-pur-etale-tower-brown-adjunction]. The transpose of the actual ordinary-system reduction of $t_S$ is an isomorphism
$$\theta_S:\mathcal R_XM_S\xrightarrow{\sim}\nu_{X,\bullet}^*G_S^{\mathrm{et}}R\nu_{Y,\bullet,*}\mathcal R_YL_S,$$
whose evaluations are precisely those finite transposes. Its etale Brown output is bounded below, so the displayed site transport is defined. In particular the actual-system-isomorphism alternative holds over $H$, even if only single-degree concentration held over $E$. Rationalization gives the representing Hom bijections for every condensed $H$-test object. For finite $E\subset H\subset H'$, these bijections commute with scalar extension; the reconstructed counits are the scalar extensions of $t$ with their specified tensor associators and compact-support comparisons. All assertions are natural in actual supplied-system morphisms; no degree-concentration assertion after a nonflat quotient is imposed.

source.place: Localized integral Hom formula, and agent finite-extension argument needed for sk-thm-sp-qbar/sk-thm-sp-qbar.proof.md; returned item proof Steps 8–10, including ramified cofinal quotients and the transpose of the extended counit.

proof.text: For the ordinary finite-coordinate prerequisites, restriction along the quotient-ring equivalence is an additive equivalence. Compare the remaining realization with restriction along the constant ring sheafification unit by constantCommuteCompose and its unit equation. Apply [lem-cbc-constant-ring-module-sheaves] to obtain an equivalence; additivity and finite exactness follow. For a ramified quotient, naturality of the constant sheafification unit and the inverse quotient-ring equivalence identify the two scalar actions on every section. The identity additive map is therefore linear, natural, invertible, and is uniquely determined by its identity-on-sections normalization. These arguments prove finiteOrdinary_properties and restrictionSquare_existsUnique; the derived normalization and the later scalar-extension argument remain to be formalized.

Write $\tau$ for the representing map called $t$ in the statement, reserving $t$ for the uniformizer. Apply [lem-pur-integral-reconstructed-representing-pair] to the supplied data, in whichever alternative holds. Its $R$-linear natural bijection $\beta_K$ sends $h:K\to M$ to $\tau\circ P_R(h)$: naturality in $K$, applied to $h$ and $1_M$, gives this formula. Its reduction satisfies $\tau_n=\epsilon_{A_n}\circ F_{A_n}(\phi_n)$. Apply [lem-pur-integral-reduction-uniform-tor] to $M$ on $X$ and $L$ on $Y$ separately. Their reductions lie in the finite constructible finite-Tor categories, with compatible etale-origin witnesses and common finite bounds. Thus every finite coefficient mate used below has an input in its stated domain.

source.place: Integral Hom chain used in the rational Hom display; domain check for the finite-extension supplement.

proof.text:
For $C=J_X(K[1/t])$, tensor $\beta_K$ and its inverse with $E$. Their composites remain identities, so this gives an isomorphism of localized Hom groups. By [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization] and the compact-support realization $a$ of [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization], it is the desired map
$$\operatorname{Hom}_E(C,M_E^c)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_E(P_E^cC,L_E^c),\qquad h\longmapsto \tau_E\circ P_E^c(h).$$
Here $\tau_E=J_Y(\tau[1/t])\circ a_{f,E,M}^{-1}$. Naturality for a fractional arrow $u/t^q$ follows by multiplying the integral naturality equation by $t^{-q}$. Every condensed test object is isomorphic to such a $C$ by essential surjectivity of $J_X$. Conjugating by this isomorphism extends the bijection to it; two choices agree because their comparison is a morphism in the full localized category, for which naturality was just proved. Evaluating at $1_{M_E^c}$ gives precisely $\tau_E$.

source.place: The displayed localized Hom chain and the following counit paragraph.

proof.text:
Fix $H/E$, $S,v,e$ as in the statement. By [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], ordinary extension of $M,L$ agrees via the specified completion maps with completed integral extension, and the outputs are derived complete. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-constructible-scalar-transport] these outputs belong to $\mathcal I_X(S),\mathcal I_Y(S)$. Apply [lem-pur-integral-reduction-uniform-tor] over $H$ to these outputs: all $v$-reductions are finite constructible finite-Tor with common bounds and compatible site witnesses. For $en\ge m$, balancing of tensor gives
$$(M_S)_m\cong M_n\otimes^L_{A_n}S/v^m,\qquad (L_S)_m\cong L_n\otimes^L_{A_n}S/v^m.$$
These identifications use the actual quotient projections: on a simultaneous K-flat scalar model both composites send $b\otimes(a\otimes x)$ to $ba\otimes x$. Their derived compatibility is [lem-pur-system-scalar-coherence]. By the coefficient compatibility of $\alpha$ and the integral compact-support scalar comparison in [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization], reduction of $\tau_S$ is the coefficient extension of $\tau_n$ conjugated by the finite projection comparison, for every such factorization.

source.place: Finite-field extension supplement to the localized Hom argument: actual scalar models and quotient cocones.

proof.text:
Put $B=S/t^nS=S/v^{en}$ and $T=-\otimes^L_{A_n}B$. Use $q:T_YF_{A_n}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_BT_X$ and $b:T_XG_{A_n}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_BT_Y$ from [lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons]. The finite transpose of $(\tau_S)_{en}$ is
$$d_{en}=b_{L_n}\circ T_X(\phi_n).$$
Indeed the counit equation for $b$ and naturality of $q$ give
$$\epsilon_B\circ F_B(d_{en})=T_Y(\epsilon_{A_n}\circ F_{A_n}(\phi_n))\circ q_{M_n}^{-1}=T_Y(\tau_n)\circ q_{M_n}^{-1}.$$
The last map is $(\tau_S)_{en}$ by Step 3. Uniqueness of the adjunction transpose proves the formula, and both factors of $d_{en}$ are isomorphisms. Step 1 supplies the required finite-Tor domains; no assertion about a global integral exceptional functor is used.

source.place: Finite-extension supplement: finite-free cofinal levels and the counit-normalized mate identity.

proof.text:
For arbitrary $m\ge1$, choose $n$ with $en\ge m$. Apply the same counit equation to the quotient $S/v^{en}\to S/v^m$, now using [lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons] with coefficient field $H$. By Step 3, $(\tau_S)_m$ is the quotient extension of $(\tau_S)_{en}$ with its projection comparison. Its transpose is consequently
$$d_m=b_{en,m}\circ(d_{en}\otimes^L_{S/v^{en}}S/v^m),$$
using the normalization of the reductions of $M_S,L_S$. Tensor is a functor and preserves isomorphisms even though this quotient need not be flat; hence $d_m$ is invertible. For two choices $n,n'$, choose $N\ge n,n'$. The mixed quotient/finite-free cocycle for $b$ and $q$ identifies both formulas with the one from level $eN$. Alternatively each is the unique transpose of the same $(\tau_S)_m$. This proves the asserted cofinal independence and quotient compatibility without imposing cohomological concentration after quotienting.

source.place: Finite-extension supplement: all uniformizer levels, quotient mates and common further comparisons.

proof.text:
Set $B_\bullet=\mathcal R_XM_S$ and $C_\bullet=\mathcal R_YL_S$. They are normalized actual derived systems by [lem-pur-normalized-reconstruction-adjunction-calculus], and bounded below of etale origin by Step 3. The isomorphisms $d_m$ identify $Rf_m^!(C_m)$ with $B_m$, so these exceptional images have a common lower bound. Apply [lem-pur-brown-tower-finite-site-comparison] over $H$: the etale Brown output is bounded below, its site transport $N_S$ exists, and the transported Brown Hom bijection applies to $B_\bullet,C_\bullet$. Form the actual system map
$$a_S:F_SB_\bullet\xrightarrow{\alpha_{M_S}^{-1}}\mathcal R_YP_SM_S\xrightarrow{\mathcal R_Y(\tau_S)}C_\bullet.$$
Here the comparison $\alpha$ is an actual system isomorphism by [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization]. Define $\theta_S:B_\bullet\to N_S$ as the transported Brown transpose of $a_S$. The counit-preserving evaluation comparisons of the Brown lemma identify its evaluations with the $d_m$ of Steps 4–5. These are invertible, so $\theta_S$ is invertible by the evaluation criterion of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Thus one actual system isomorphism has been constructed; no lifting of an arbitrary family of evaluated morphisms is invoked.

source.place: Integral Hom-chain supplement: transpose the scalar-extended actual counit, then detect its invertibility by evaluation.

proof.text: Use the actual-system-isomorphism alternative of [lem-pur-integral-reconstructed-representing-pair] over $H$, with supplied system $B_\bullet$, identification $\theta_S$, and reconstruction $M_S\cong\mathcal L_XB_\bullet$. The last is the actual unit isomorphism of [lem-pur-normalized-reconstruction-adjunction-calculus]; Step 3 verifies all constructibility and bound hypotheses. This gives integral representing bijections. Their reconstructed counit $\tau'_S$ is $\tau_S$: under $\alpha$, its reduction is the Brown counit composed with $F_S(\theta_S)$, which is $a_S$ by definition of transpose. The reduction/limit counit in that reconstruction cancels the reduction/limit unit by the triangle identity. Thus $\mathcal R_Y(\tau'_S)=\mathcal R_Y(\tau_S)$ as actual system maps. Reduction is fully faithful on derived-complete objects by the same reconstruction calculus, so the integral maps coincide. Repeating Step 2 with $H$ gives the representing Hom bijection for every condensed $H$-test object and with counit the realization of $\tau_S$. This works also when the original datum used only the single-degree alternative.

source.place: Integral Hom-chain and counit normalization, then the rational Hom chain over each finite extension.

proof.text: For $E\subset H\subset H'$, the ordinary tensor associator identifies $(M_S)_{S'}$ with $M_{S'}$ and likewise for $L$. Its compatibility with the specified completed scalar comparisons, including units and cofinal choices, is [lem-fix-scalar-completion-associator]. The compact-support scalar comparisons obey the same composition equation by [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization]. Therefore both constructions of the extended counit give $(\tau\otimes_R1_S)\otimes_S1_{S'}=\tau\otimes_R1_{S'}$, conjugated by these very associators and compact-support comparisons. For a morphism $h$ the representing bijection is $h\mapsto\tau\circ P(h)$ (Steps 1–2,7); applying scalar extension sends it to $h_{H}\mapsto\tau_H\circ P_H(h_H)$. This proves commutation of the Hom bijections with scalar extension, transitively, including fractional arrows after rationalization. For actual supplied-system morphisms the integral counit squares hold by [lem-pur-integral-reconstructed-representing-pair]. Applying the scalar functors and then $J$ preserves these equalities, so the constructed bijections and counits have the claimed naturality. The actual Brown transposes inherit that naturality by transposition of the actual system counit squares.

source.place: Finite-extension supplement for sk-thm-sp-qbar: transitivity of the actual extended counits and naturality, before taking any coefficient colimit.

proof_origin.place: Displayed localized Hom chain; finite-extension and ordinary Brown-system argument written from the cited existing DAG interfaces. No global integral right adjoint is assumed. V6 formalized the ordinary finite-coordinate equivalence and unique restriction square using the constant-ring module-sheaf equivalence; all existing later proof steps are retained.
